claim.why_it_matters: Every sub-entry indent on this page is dropped: the markdown emits all lines flush left, whereas the PDF indents sub-entries under their parent heading. The parent/child relation is the whole information content of an index entry - 'METHOD-ID paragraph 269' as a top-level entry means something different from 'METHOD-ID paragraph 269' as a sub-entry of 'Method-name'. Pages 1247, 1248, 1253, 1255 and 1256 of the same index DO carry the indents (as '    '), so the loss is an inconsistency within the transcription itself, not a deliberate style choice.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against a 300 dpi render of PDF sheet 1249 (printed folio 1219) and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. (1) The printed page carries two distinct left edges per column. Cropping and enlarging the left column shows 'LOCK ON MULTIPLE clause' and 'LOCK phrase' starting at the column margin, while 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 312', 'LOCK MODE clause 325', 'READ statement 692', 'REWRITE statement 710' and 'WRITE statement 786' all start at a clearly deeper indent stop. The right-column crop is decisive: 'Method-definition 259', 'METHOD-ID paragraph 269' and 'Method-name 98, 102' sit at the margin, while the SECOND 'METHOD-ID paragraph 269' and 'Scope of 149' sit at the indent stop. So the PDF prints 'METHOD-ID paragraph 269' twice on this page with two different meanings - once as a top-level entry filed alphabetically between 'Method-definition' and 'Method-name', once as a sub-entry of 'Method-name'. (2) The markdown for page 1249 renders both occurrences byte-identically at column 0 (lines 66 and 68 of the extracted page), so the two entries become indistinguishable and the parent/child relation is destroyed. This is genuine information loss, not reflow, hyphenation, or page-break furniture: no marker of any kind survives. (3) Both quotations in the claim are accurate - I diffed the claim's markdown block against specs/ISO_COBOL.md and it matches verbatim, and the claim's rendering of the PDF indentation matches what the glyphs show. (4) The self-inconsistency is confirmed mechanically: counting ' ' occurrences per page segment in specs/ISO_COBOL.md gives 1247=104, 1248=212, 1253=180, 1255=192, 1256=148, but 1249=0. Page 1249's segment is also markedly shorter (3889 chars vs ~5200 for its indent-carrying neighbours), consistent with ~1.3 kB of indent markup having been dropped. Sampling page 1248 shows the intended encoding is a literal '    ' prefix. Nothing about page 1249 differs in kind from 1248 or 1253 - it is the same two-column index in the same typography - so the flush-left output is a transcription defect, not a style choice. Approximately 38 sub-entry lines on this page lose their subordination (about 16 in the left column, about 22 in the right).
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with two corrections to the framing. (a) The 'kind' label is imprecise: nothing is misplaced or relocated. The defect is LOST STRUCTURE - the four-space (rendered '    ') sub-entry indent that encodes index subordination is stripped from every line on the page, flattening a two-level index into a one-level list. Severity 'structural' is correct. (b) The blast radius is larger than one page. Page 1249 is not an isolated lapse: the same zero-' ' signature covers the contiguous run 1249, 1250, 1251 and 1252 (nbsp counts 0/0/0/0, segment lengths 3889/3949/4128/3902), bracketed by indent-carrying pages 1247-1248 before it and 1253 after it. Any fix should re-extract the whole 1249-1252 run, not page 1249 alone. The sharpest single instance of the harm on 1249 is the doubled 'METHOD-ID paragraph 269': the PDF prints it once as a top-level entry and once, indented, as a sub-entry of 'Method-name', and the markdown collapses the two into identical adjacent lines that read as an accidental duplicate. A comparable collapse hits 'Definition 241', which the PDF indents as a sub-entry of 'Method resolution signature' (the parent is the last line of the left column, the child the first line of the right); in the markdown the two are separated only by a blank line and the child now reads as a top-level entry.
